question.text: Why does use of currency futures for hedging gold ETF investment NOT completely remove USDINR spot risk?

answer.text: Because futures price depends on both spot price AND premium/discount, which also changes
Because gold ETF and USDINR are unrelated
Because futures contracts are only available for 1 month
Because the lot size doesn't match the investment amount exactly

explanation.text: The Logic: For the gold ETF hedge, the currency futures price is a function of spot price and premium/discount. Futures reduce the embedded USDINR spot risk, but the hedge can remain imperfect because the USDINR premium/discount can change over the contract period. The Trap: Lot size mismatch is a separate operational issue. The main reason for imperfect hedging here is that futures prices also depend on changes in the USDINR premium/discount. Note: Customized forwards can sometimes provide better hedges because they can be tailored to the exposure (see pp.61 and 125). Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, pp.61, 99, and 125.
